newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller backed in corruption charge.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller backed in corruption charge.

text.p: A parliamentary commission on Monday rejected a bid to send Turkey's deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, to the Supreme Court on corruption charges stemming from her time as head of the government.
"A decision was taken, by 13 votes for and two abstentions, that it was not necessary for Ciller to go to the Supreme Court," commission head Metin Bostancioglu told reporters.
The commission recommended that MPs vote within the next two weeks against sending Ciller, Turkey's first woman leader, to the highest court in the land.
She had been accused of failing to prevent contract irregularities at the TEDAS state-run electricity company in her time as prime minister from 1993 until earlier this year.
The TEDAS allegation is the least serious of three corruption charges against Ciller, a pro-Western secularist now in coalition with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.
Political analysts say Ciller would be freer to oppose Erbakan from within the government, or even break the coalition, if all the charges were dropped.
She relies on Erbakan's backing to avoid trial at the supreme court on suspicion of graft, the analysts say.

Two other commissions will rule in the coming weeks on investigations into Ciller's substantial wealth and allegations that she interfered in the sale of state-owned car manufacturer TOFAS to help business allies.
